properties.name: Advice
properties.webBody:
This Advice is being issued for Guildford and Yapeen. 
  • Coliban Water has advised that as of Thursday 20 August, the tap water at Guildford and Yapeen is not safe to drink without boiling first. 
  • A burst water main occurred in Guildford late on Wednesday night.
  • This burst caused a supply interruption and low water pressure in both towns.
  • Low water pressure and interruptions to water supply can lead to a build-up of bacteria that can make people sick.
If you live or work within Guildford and Yapeen, you must boil tap water before drinking. 
What you should do:  
  • Boil water before drinking it, or drink bottled water.
  • Boil water for food preparation, cleaning fruit and vegetables, making ice and for preparing baby formula.
  • Boil water for brushing teeth. 
To ensure water is safe, you should: 
  • Heat water until a continuous and rapid stream of air-bubbles is produced from the bottom of a pan or kettle (kettles with automatic shut-off switches are suitable). 
  • Allow water to cool before use. 
  • Store water in a clean, closed container for later use. 
  • Be careful when boiling water to prevent scalding or burns.
  • If you are concerned that you may have been affected by contaminated water, contact your doctor or Nurse-on-Call. 
Impacts in your area: 
  • Coliban Water is working to restore drinking water in the town. You will not have tap water until it is restored.
  • Once water is restored, you need to boil it before drinking.
  • Drinking water can be sourced from:
  • John Powell Reserve, Midland Highway, Guildford.
  • 1 Templeton Street, Guildford, next to the old General Store.
  • Testing will need to occur once the water supply is back. This may take a few days.
This message was issued by Department of Health.

The next update is expected by 21/08/2026 06:10 pm or as the situation changes.

properties.name: Watch & Act
properties.webBody:
This Moderate Flood Warning is being issued for the Loddon River upstream of Laanecoorie.

  • Moderate flooding is occurring at Bet Bet, with minor flooding occurring at Newstead.
  • 38.4mm of rain has fallen at Bet Bet in the 48 hours to 8:00am on Thursday.
  • At 11:00am on Thursday 20 August, the Bet Bet Creek at Bet Bet was at 5.17 metres, above the moderate flood level (5.00 metres).
  • At 11:00am on Thursday 20 August, the Loddon River at Newstead was at 2.87 metres, falling below the minor flood level (3.00 metres).
Stay safe - avoid the flooded area. Be aware of potential hazards caused by flooding and never enter floodwater.
What you should do:
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never enter floodwater.
  • If you are camping close to a creek or river, you may be at risk of flooding and need to move to higher ground, away from waterways.
  • Stay informed by listening to emergency broadcasters and monitoring warnings.
If you choose to leave:
  • Remember to take your pets, mobile phone, spare clothes and medications.
  • Travel to the home of family or friends who are in a safe location, away from flooding.
  • Turn off gas and electricity at your home or workplace.
  • Be aware of any road closures when you leave.
If you are travelling:
  • Do not enter flooded areas. Turn around a find a safe alternative route.
  • Be aware of road hazards including mud, debris and damaged roads or bridges.
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never drive, walk or ride through floodwater.
If you stay or if it is unsafe to leave:
  • Make sure you have enough food, drinking water, medications and pet food to survive for three to five days in case you become isolated.
  • Use plugs, sandbags or household items to block toilets, sinks and drains to stop sewerage backflow.
  • Lift it - move valuables and vital household items up on high surfaces, such as on top of tables, chairs, benches and beds.
Impacts in your area:
  • Be aware of water over roads. Do not drive, walk or play in floodwater.
  • Check the VicTraffic website (www.traffic.transport.vic.gov.au) for road closures and follow instructions from emergency services.
  • Stagnant water can be harmful to your health. Don’t swim, drink or wash in stagnant water.
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

The next update is expected by 21/08/2026 01:00 pm or as the situation changes.

Use multiple sources to stay informed:

- Minor flooding is possible at Barham.
- The Murray River at Barham is currently at 5.43 metres and steady, below the minor flood level.
- It may exceed the minor flood level (5.50 metres) from overnight Thursday into Friday.
- Further rises are possible as upstream flows arrive next week.


Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and remain alert.

properties.webBody:
This Minor Flood Warning is being issued for the Kiewa River downstream of Mongans Bridge at Bandiana.

Renewed minor flooding possible at Bandiana from Thursday afternoon

Rainfall forecast for the remainder of Thursday and into Friday is likely to cause renewed river level rises along the Kiewa River. 

Minor flooding is possible at Bandiana Thursday afternoon.

Kiewa River downstream of Mongans Bridge

Renewed minor flooding is possible along the Kiewa River at Bandiana.

The Kiewa River at Bandiana is 2.36m, as at 12.32pm on 20 Aug, and steady which is below the minor flood level. The Kiewa River at Bandiana may reach around the minor flood level (2.80 m) Thursday afternoon
Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and remain alert.
What you should do: 
  • Be prepared to act if your situation changes.
  • Stay informed by listening to emergency broadcasters and monitoring warnings.
  • Contact family members and neighbours to ensure they are aware of the situation.
  • Monitor weather forecasts and river levels. Go to www.bom.gov.au/vic/warnings/
Impacts in your area: 
  • For the latest road closures go to the VicTraffic website.
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

The next update is expected by 21/08/2026 02:00 pm or as the situation changes.

Use multiple sources to stay informed:
  • www.emergency.vic.gov.au
  • VicEmergency Hotline - freecall 1800 226 226
  • VicEmergency app
  • Facebook
  • Tune in to ABC Local Radio, commercial and designated community radio stations, or News24 TV.
Accessibility: 
The following services can help you, or someone you know, access information during an emergency. 
  • To access this information in other languages, call the Translating and Interpreting Service on 131 450 (freecall) and ask them to call VicEmergency Hotline. 
  • If you are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech/communication impairment, contact the National Relay Service and ask them to call the VicEmergency Hotline.
